requirements_slice.system_goal: Reuse the existing compact Week DEV chip as a dev-only runtime diagnostics disclosure without changing Week content, backend payloads, scoring, or production behavior.

in_scope.item: Reuse the existing shell DEV/PROD chip on /week as the only runtime-disclosure entry point.
Keep the collapsed chip visually compact and local to the chip area.
In non-production on /week, expand and collapse a local disclosure that shows Week render path, bootstrap result, and current mode from existing page and runtime state.
Derive Week render-path labels from existing Week page states only: loading, auth_gate, empty, in_progress, error, canonical.
Add targeted unit, Playwright, visual, and packet-local read-only evidence for the dev-expanded and prod-unchanged Week states.

out_of_scope.item: Any new payload field, scoring change, Week explainability change, or business-logic change.
Any new top-level banner or separate diagnostics screen.
Any diagnostics field beyond render path, bootstrap result, and current mode.

use_case.summary: Inspect the active Week runtime lane from the existing compact chip without leaving the Week surface.
use_case.scenario: On /week in non-production, tapping the compact chip expands a local disclosure with Week render path, bootstrap result, and runtime mode.
Tapping the chip again collapses the disclosure and restores the compact local state.
In production and on non-Week routes, the chip remains visually unchanged and inert and no diagnostics block appears.
Targeted verification records packet-local evidence, including a read-only post-test verdict and the local artifact identifiers for the Week helper slice.

business_invariants.invariant: The disclosure is client-local helper UI only and must not add backend requests or payload fields.
Only render path, bootstrap result, and current mode may appear in the visible disclosure body.
Interactive behavior is limited to non-production on /week; production and non-Week routes remain inert.
Week render-path labels are derived from existing page states rather than new backend DTO fields or diagnostics endpoints.
Week hero, day strip, day drawer, domain, actions, explainability, deep sections, CTA, and WeekBrief contracts remain unchanged.
This helper slice owns packet-local evidence only and does not claim canonical Today or Week runtime closeout.

expected_failure_handling.item: If any diagnostics source is absent, render a stable unknown or unavailable value instead of blocking /week.
If the page is between Week states, the disclosure may show loading or unknown, but it must not crash or leak raw objects.
If the shared shell badge cannot stay bounded to / and /week without leaking interaction to other routes, stop and escalate before widening the feature.
If no dedicated production Playwright host is available, deterministic unit proof is the minimum acceptable production-inert lane.
If packet-local evidence is missing or the read-only post-test review ends as no-evidence-blocker, the wave remains blocked until the evidence bundle is attributable.

known_defects.defect: DEFECT-SLICE-WEEK-1: The shared shell badge already emits a /week toggle request, but the Week-side helper contract is not yet fully aligned as a stable disclosure lane.
DEFECT-SLICE-WEEK-2: The current Week page does not expose a dedicated render-path helper label, so implementation must derive one from existing page states without redefining Week contracts.

success_criteria.criterion: The Week chip stays compact in collapsed state.
In non-production on /week, tapping the chip expands and collapses a local disclosure.
The disclosure shows render path, bootstrap result, and current mode only.
Week render-path labels stay stable across loading, auth_gate, empty, in_progress, error, and canonical branches.
Production and non-Week routes stay visually and behaviorally unchanged.
Verifier evidence includes dev-collapsed, dev-expanded, and prod-unchanged Week proof.
Packet-local evidence is explicit, attributable to the Week helper lane, and the read-only post-test review is clean or degraded-but-expected.
